## Example 3.6 {#fv3-example-3-6 .fv-lesson .line-lesson }

```{=html}
<div data-module="hinge" data-correct="3" class="hinge numeric-choices"><p class="hinge-question">What is the Cartesian equation of the line <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{r}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\3\end{bmatrix}+\lambda\begin{bmatrix}-2\\4\end{bmatrix}"></span>?</p><div class="choices"><button class="choice" data-answer="1" aria-pressed="false"><b>1</b><span><span data-math="2y+x=7"></span></span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="2" aria-pressed="false"><b>2</b><span><span data-math="y-2x=-5"></span></span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="3" aria-pressed="false"><b>3</b><span><span data-math="y+2x=5"></span></span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="4" aria-pressed="false"><b>4</b><span><span data-math="2y-x=-1"></span></span></button></div><div class="hinge-bottom"><p>Fist on chest. Think quietly.<br>On “show”, hold up 1–4 fingers.</p><button class="reveal-answer primary">Reveal answer</button></div><div class="hinge-explanation" hidden><strong>3.</strong> <span data-math="m=4/(-2)=-2"></span> and the line passes through <span data-math="(1,3)"></span>.</div></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Example 3.6 · p. 47 · 2020 HSC Extension 2 Q3 (1 mark)</div>

::: {.notes}
1–4 correspond to A–D; correct 3 (C). x=1−2λ, y=3+4λ, so y+2x=5. Choice 1 uses reciprocal gradient −1/2. Choice 2 loses the negative sign and uses an incorrect constant. Choice 4 uses a positive reciprocal gradient and an incorrect constant. (1,3) also satisfies choice 1, so direction is essential. Ready: Example 3.7. Divided: compare direction ratios. Needs explanation: use y−3=−2(x−1).
:::
